title: Plancherel and the directional-derivative identity on Schwartz space
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with its Borel measurable structure and Lebesgue measure, and let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. A Schwartz function $f:V\to H$ is smooth and satisfies $\sup_x\|x\|^k\|D^n f(x)\|<\infty$ for all nonnegative integers $k,n$. Define $\widehat f(\xi)=\int_V e^{-2\pi i\langle x,\xi\rangle}f(x)\,dx$. Then $$\int_V\|\widehat f(\xi)\|^2\,d\xi=\int_V\|f(x)\|^2\,dx.$$ For every $v\in V$, with $D_v f(x)=Df(x)[v]$, one also has $$\widehat{D_v f}(\xi)=2\pi i\langle\xi,v\rangle\widehat f(\xi).$$
